name: Shethar (One of the seven princes of Persia and Media who were closest to King Ahasuerus)
title: Persian prince at the court of Ahasuerus
summary: Shethar was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had direct access to King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I). These seven princes held the highest positions in the Persian Empire and were consulted when the king wanted to know what the law required regarding Queen Vashti, who had refused to obey the king's command. Shethar is mentioned only in the book of Esther and represents the Persian power structure surrounding the Jewish diaspora.

keyEvents.title: Queen Vashti's disobedience
keyEvents.description: King Ahasuerus held a great feast and sent his seven court officials to bring Queen Vashti, but she refused to come. This created a crisis at the court.

keyEvents.title: The King Consults the Seven Princes
keyEvents.description: After Vashti's refusal, King Ahasuerus asked the seven princes of Persia and Media, including Shethar, what the law required should be done with the queen.

keyEvents.title: Shethar Mentioned Among the Seven Princes
keyEvents.description: Shethar is named as one of the seven princes who stood closest to the king and held the highest seats in the kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Memucan's Advice on Behalf of the Princes
keyEvents.description: Memucan, one of the seven princes, spoke on behalf of the group and advised the king to depose Vashti and choose a new queen, advice that was followed.
